subject: 0205C34A1561E7B0B0C576B17640B5A9
introduction: “In this Cause of God there is no secret doctrine or secret society or club or gathering.” The Bahá’í writings forbid secret meetings among the believers and, in later guidance, ask Bahá’ís to withdraw from Freemasonry and similar orders: not because such bodies are thought evil, but because a Faith addressed to everyone cannot have an inner circle or a divided loyalty. Jesus’s “in secret have I said nothing”, the Buddha’s open hand and Paul’s “not done in a corner” make the same claim for their teaching. Yet Jesus also spoke of “mysteries” given to some, and Paul of “hidden wisdom”, and the attraction of the esoteric is old.
questions: Why would secrecy among believers be forbidden even when the motives are pure?
What is the difference between depth and secrecy?
Reading 6 and reading 10 give different advice about membership. How do you account for the difference?

outside.why: In the Cause of God there must be no secret gathering. Jesus to the high priest: I spake openly to the world; in secret have I said nothing.
Counterfeits of religion. Men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
A meeting formed to keep secrets. There is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.
Clandestine societies being organized. Paul before the king: this thing was not done in a corner.

A questioner told not to dissociate herself from her society. The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s advice here differs from the later guidance in readings 10 to 12. What had changed?

The message is for all, none of it for a circle of initiates. The Buddha: I have preached the truth without making any distinction between exoteric and esoteric doctrine; the Tathagata has no such thing as the closed fist of a teacher.

Jesus did speak of an inner circle: it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. Is there a difference between teaching that only some can grasp and teaching that only some may hear?
No secret doctrine, society or club. What ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.

Nothing intrinsically wrong with Masonry. Paul’s language was adopted by every esoteric movement since: we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom. What draws people to hidden wisdom, and what do the readings offer in its place?
Bahá’ís urged to withdraw from old affiliations. No man can serve two masters.
The friends should not enter secret societies. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel.

shortfall: Readings 5 and 11 are a personal reply and an administrative rule; one companion fewer was placed than the guide has quotations.
